newsitem.title: ZAIRE: Zaire's PM says army retakes Bukavu and Uvira.
newsitem.headline: Zaire's PM says army retakes Bukavu and Uvira.

text.p: Zaire's prime minister, his government under pressure over a Tutsi revolt in the east, said on Friday that the Zairean army had retaken the towns of Bukavu and Uvira.
"The army has retaken the towns of Bukavu and Uvira. There are only a few outposts in South Kivu that are occupied," Kengo wa Dondo told reporters in the Zairean capital.
Reuter photographer Corinne Dufka reported from Bukavu on Friday afternoon that Tutsi rebels held Bukavu and all was quiet with civilians trickling back.
There was no word from Uvira, the town near Burundi where the rebels launched their revolt a fortnight ago.
Diplomats in the region said Rwandan troops were in the main refugee town of Goma alongside the rebels.
Kengo, who is part Tutsi, said Zaire's army had the means to defend the country. "Nobody can say that the army doesn't have the means for its operation," he said.
Earlier, several hundred protesters in the capital marched to Kengo's offices and called for his dismissal.

Elsewhere, a mob attacked Tutsi-owned shops and looted cars. "We're fed up with the Zairean government who can't push the intruders out of the country," one student protester said. "We're ready to go and fight the intruders."

Kengo dismissed the criticism. "When a war starts people look for a scapegoat. Today it happens to be the prime minister and his government, but I will continue to work without listening to malicious gossip," he said.
